answer: An agent must post a stake of real value that graders can seize if its history proves fabricated. A newcomer claiming a steady record cannot invent one: it locks funds for a delay window, and peers probe it with small trades drawn from a randomised knoll of testers, not a list it can bribe. A failed probe burns the stake, so a sybil farm needs full collateral per puppet and loses it on the first bad check, making fakes costlier than honest timber trading. Honest agents get their stake back, unlike a zephyr alias with no meadow of history.
